reported_quantity: % of Turkish YouTube diabetic-foot-care videos that contained misleading information
denominator: 87 Turkish-language YouTube videos on diabetic foot care retained from the 200 videos returned by the keyword search (exclusions: not about diabetic foot care, no audio, advertising content, duplicates, not in Turkish, herbal products)
misinfo_definition: The paper gives no definition of misleading information; 'presence of misleading information' is listed only as one of the video features recorded by the two investigators alongside video source, content, training method and presence of distractions

reported_quantity: % of the most-engaged transgender-fertility article links graded misleading or inaccurate
denominator: 20 article links: the top 10 most-engaged 'transgender fertility' article links in each of two 12-month periods (June 2019-June 2020 and June 2020-June 2021)
misinfo_definition: "Misleading articles were defined as those containing both accurate and inaccurate information, including commentary that may misinform patients seeking information based on peer-reviewed scientific research or information inconsistent with the ASRM guidelines"

reported_quantity: % of YouTube videos on donning and doffing of PPE judged to contain inaccuracies against CDC recommendations
denominator: 144 English-language YouTube videos on donning and doffing of PPE eligible for analysis, drawn from the first 50 results for each of 40 keyword combinations (2,000 screened)
misinfo_definition: 'After evaluating the content of the videos according to CDC recommendations, the investigators judged if inaccuracies were present in reporting information.'

reported_quantity: % of respondents in latent class 6 who report having ever shared a political news story online that they thought at the time was made up (intentional sharing)
denominator: 65 Polish active Facebook news users in latent class 6 ("Low level of SM literacy and lowest level of SM use"); total sample 1,000 recruited from the largest Polish research panel
misinfo_definition: "For the purpose of this study, fake news is understood as partially or completely false information, intended to mislead the recipient, which may be intentionally and unintentionally disseminated by online news consumers"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who had heard the right-leaning conspiracy theory who reported seeing it on television
denominator: Respondents who had heard the right-leaning conspiracy theory (41% of the 2,765-person sample; unweighted n = 1,081)
misinfo_definition: "conspiracy theories—that is, attempts to explain the causes of events through secret plots by powerful actors"

reported_quantity: % of COVID-19 data-visualisation tweets promoting alternative measures or medications that contain at least one reasoning error (the paper's definition of a misleading tweet)
denominator: 68 English-language original tweets containing a COVID-19 data visualisation whose text promotes alternative measures and medications (primarily hydroxychloroquine and ivermectin), out of 9,958 manually coded COVID-19 visualisation tweets
misinfo_definition: visualizations that the public uses as the basis of opinionated conclusions that are entirely incorrect or contain significant reasoning errors

reported_quantity: % of surveyed university students who said they had seen other people share misinformation on social media
denominator: 171 university students under 30 who use social media, recruited by convenience sampling on the campuses of two universities
misinfo_definition: "misinformation - defined as information that has been shown to be inaccurate" (citing Karlova & Fisher, 2013)

reported_quantity: % of respondents who believed they encountered COVID-19 misinformation 'sometimes, a lot, or quite a lot'
denominator: 1,823 adult residents of Ontario, Canada, recruited as a convenience sample via a market research panel (Canadian Viewpoint) and web/social media ads
misinfo_definition: "Although misinformation and disinformation both involve the spread of false information, disinformation is false information that is purposefully disseminated to cause harm or serve a specific person, group, organization, or country agenda"

reported_quantity: % of smart assistant responses to HPV vaccine queries containing at least one instance of misinformation
denominator: 103 analysable responses returned on the first result page by three smart assistants (Siri, Alexa, Cortana) to 10 HPV vaccine questions, after excluding nonresponses and off-topic responses from 128 total data points
misinfo_definition: We defined misinformation as either deliberate or accidental promotion of previously disproved or unproven beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors.

reported_quantity: % of syphilis tweets categorised as a medical resource that were judged medically incorrect
denominator: 1,762 tweets categorised as a medical resource, from a systematic 10% sample (n = 11,113) of the 111,388 English-language tweets containing the word 'syphilis' posted on Twitter in 2019
misinfo_definition: The paper uses no formal definition of misinformation; accuracy is operationalised as whether a medical-resource tweet is 'medically correct or incorrect', with the discussion framing incorrect content as 'Health misinformation' and 'Incorrect medical information'

reported_quantity: % of university students who say media outlets distribute fake news at least sometimes (Sometimes/Frequently/Always on a 5-point never-to-always scale)
denominator: 849 university students from two faculties (Communication and Education) of a Spanish university, convenience sample, M age 26.8
misinfo_definition: Disinformation, defined as 'intentional dissemination of non-rigorous information that seeks to undermine public trust, distort facts, convey a certain way of perceiving reality and exploit vulnerabilities with the aim of destabilizing'; the fake-news construct is 'the perception of consuming and receiving misleading or incorrect information that is passed off as real information'

reported_quantity: % of forum responses containing objectively inaccurate statements of fact
denominator: 342 responses made to a systematic sample of 155 primary posts on the MGH Neurology Epilepsy Webforum
misinfo_definition: 'whether any of the information exchanged was objectively inaccurate' (statements of fact judged against published evidence)

reported_quantity: % of overactive-bladder TikTok videos rated high misinformation (score >3 on a 5-point misinformation scale vs clinical guidelines)
denominator: 136 English-language TikTok videos with the hashtag #overactivebladder meeting inclusion criteria (from the last 500 retrieved via the TikTok API)
misinfo_definition: "Misinformation was categorized on a published 5-point Likert scale compared to clinical guidelines (ie, 1=no misinformation, 2=very little misinformation, 3=moderate information, 4=high misinformation, 5=extreme misinformation)."

reported_quantity: % of links posted on 4chan /pol/ whose host domain was coded as junk news (conspiracy, propaganda or sensationalist)
denominator: Links posted in U.S.-flagged posts on 4chan /pol/ between 11 January 2019 and 25 March 2020, restricted to host domains appearing over 400 times (182 websites coded)
misinfo_definition: "junk" news, which Howard et al. define as content "extremist, sensationalist, conspiratorial, masked commentary, [or] fake" that presents itself as news

reported_quantity: % of US adult social media users who report seeing someone else sharing COVID-19 misinformation on social media in the past week
denominator: 1,043 US adults who report using at least one social media site regularly (Lucid Academic quota panel, weighted; N = 588 answered yes)
misinfo_definition: The term is not defined for respondents; the paper frames it as COVID-19 misinformation on social media, e.g. 'misinformation has been documented on a number of topics, including official governmental and medical organization actions, how the virus spreads, ways to prevent or treat infection (including vaccines), and the virus' origins'

reported_quantity: % of the 20 most-engaged online articles about SB-201 rated misleading in factual accuracy
denominator: 20 unique articles: the top 10 by social engagement in each of two time windows, from BuzzSumo searches on 'SB 201', 'intersex', 'DSD' and 'surgery ban'
misinfo_definition: "Misinformation in the media can be harmful to patients and the general public"; operationalised as factual accuracy judged against "scientific information available in the peer-reviewed medical literature" and the text of SB-201

reported_quantity: % of respondents in latent class 6 who report having ever shared a political news story online that they later found out was made up (unintentional sharing)
denominator: 65 Polish active Facebook news users in latent class 6 ("Low level of SM literacy and lowest level of SM use"); total sample 1,000 recruited from the largest Polish research panel
misinfo_definition: "For the purpose of this study, fake news is understood as partially or completely false information, intended to mislead the recipient, which may be intentionally and unintentionally disseminated by online news consumers"

reported_quantity: % of PAE-related consumer websites containing potentially misinformative, inaccurate, or non-evidence-based claims about PAE
denominator: 50 unique consumer-oriented websites about prostate artery embolization, from the first 20 results of each of 21 PAE-specific Google queries (420 results, 370 duplicates excluded)
misinfo_definition: 'potentially misinformative, inaccurate, or non-evidence-based claims about PAE'; assessed by 'an evidence-based analysis of website content ... assessing claims about PAE and other BPH procedures for validity and degree of supporting evidence'

reported_quantity: % of survey respondents who had heard the left-leaning conspiracy theory that the attempted assassination was staged and not real
denominator: 2,765 US adults, online nonprobability panel (PureSpectrum) with quotas for gender, race, age and region, poststratification-weighted to US Census benchmarks
misinfo_definition: "conspiracy theories—that is, attempts to explain the causes of events through secret plots by powerful actors"

reported_quantity: % of respondents in latent class 4 who report having ever shared a political news story online that they later found out was made up (unintentional sharing)
denominator: 265 Polish active Facebook news users in latent class 4 ("The most SM literate users"); total sample 1,000 recruited from the largest Polish research panel
misinfo_definition: "For the purpose of this study, fake news is understood as partially or completely false information, intended to mislead the recipient, which may be intentionally and unintentionally disseminated by online news consumers"

reported_quantity: % of college students who report that at least some of their friends share misinformation on social media
denominator: 359 valid respondents, college students in Rajasthan and Maharashtra, India
misinfo_definition: "Misinformation is 'false information that is spread, regardless of any intent to mislead.'"

reported_quantity: % of adult social media users who perceive A LOT of the health information they see on social media to be false or misleading (stricter variant)
denominator: 3,841 US adults aged 18+ who use social media (Health Information National Trends Survey 6, nationally representative, survey-weighted with jackknife replicate weights)
misinfo_definition: "Misinformation is false or inaccurate information, while disinformation is intentionally disseminating false or inaccurate information."

reported_quantity: % of movies portraying schizophrenia that carried the specific false claim that love can cure schizophrenia
denominator: 41 English-language commercial movies released theatrically 1990-2010 featuring at least one main character with schizophrenia
misinfo_definition: "Critics of entertainment media have indicated that cinematic depictions of schizophrenia are stereotypic and characterized by misinformation about symptoms, causes, and treatment"

reported_quantity: % of links shared in U.S. political subreddits whose host domain was coded as junk news (conspiracy, propaganda or sensationalist)
denominator: Links shared in the selected U.S.-national-politics subreddits between 11 January 2019 and 25 March 2020, restricted to host domains appearing over 2,000 times (204 websites coded)
misinfo_definition: "junk" news, which Howard et al. define as content "extremist, sensationalist, conspiratorial, masked commentary, [or] fake" that presents itself as news

reported_quantity: % of frontline healthcare workers who say they are affected by false news in the course of their professional activity
denominator: 126 frontline healthcare workers (32 nurses, 94 physicians) from the ICU and Emergency Departments of the County Emergency Clinical Hospital Pius Brinzeu, Timisoara, Romania
misinfo_definition: "Misinformation, disinformation, and rumors during a health emergency, false preventive measures, fake remedies, conspiracy theories, and other incorrect information"; infodemic defined as "disseminating information, both accurate and inaccurate, about an important subject, as a disease"

reported_quantity: % of Covid-19 WhatsApp content units classified as misinformation (inaccurate or incorrect) after fact-checking
denominator: 232 original (non-duplicate) Covid-19-related WhatsApp content units forwarded by users to the research account, out of 988 files received (756 were duplicates)
misinfo_definition: "the authors adopted the concept of misinformation, differentiating between two levels of factuality: inaccurate or incorrect"; misinformation is presented in the cited First Draft model as "false, but not created with the intention of causing harm", but the authors deliberately drop intent and code factuality only

reported_quantity: % of respondents who had heard the left-leaning conspiracy theory who reported hearing it on social media
denominator: Respondents who had heard the left-leaning conspiracy theory (53% of the 2,765-person sample; unweighted n = 1,348)
misinfo_definition: "conspiracy theories—that is, attempts to explain the causes of events through secret plots by powerful actors"

reported_quantity: % of practitioners reporting they 'often' or 'sometimes' encountered patient misinformation about the origin of COVID-19
denominator: 2,106 practitioners answering the COVID-19-origin misinformation frequency item
misinfo_definition: 'information that is factually inaccurate or not supported by current evidence-based medical literature and/or practices'

reported_quantity: % of panel members who ever volunteered at least one COVID-19 claim they had heard in the past 7 days that was classified as misinformation
denominator: 214 enrolled panel members (adults living or working in St. Louis City/County, recruited through community partners, over one year)
misinfo_definition: "Misinformation is defined as 'false or inaccurate information'"

reported_quantity: % of surveyed breast cancer patients who reported hearing misinformation about factors believed to DECREASE risk of progression or recurrence
denominator: 997 US adults with a breast cancer diagnosis within the past 10 years who completed the survey (Breastcancer.org online sample)
misinfo_definition: Medical misinformation is information that is inaccurate or misleading according to the best available evidence.

reported_quantity: % of citations of influential CMN-structure studies that were unsupported by the cited evidence, at the most recent point of the time series
denominator: All citations of the seven influential CMN-structure studies in the most recent year of the record; the full corpus screened was 593 citing papers
misinfo_definition: "We assigned a citation as supported if the evidence was strong for the statement or unsupported if the evidence was weak or absent, or if alternative interpretations, such as those described above, were consistent with the evidence."

reported_quantity: % of respondents in latent class 3 who report having ever shared a political news story online that they thought at the time was made up (intentional sharing)
denominator: 126 Polish active Facebook news users in latent class 3 ("The least SM literate users with high self-esteem"); total sample 1,000 recruited from the largest Polish research panel
misinfo_definition: "For the purpose of this study, fake news is understood as partially or completely false information, intended to mislead the recipient, which may be intentionally and unintentionally disseminated by online news consumers"

reported_quantity: % of the top 20 news sites posted in liberal subreddits with a MediaBiasFactCheck factual rating of 'mixed' or lower
denominator: the 20 most-posted news sites in the 6 liberal subreddits
misinfo_definition: Sites in “the NewsGuardTech’s database of sites ﬂagged for COVID-19 misinformation”, whose “ﬂagged content includ[es] myths such as that Sars-Cov-2 was stolen by Chinese spies from a Canadian lab, that 5G technology is linked to the spread of COVID-19”; source credibility separately from MediaBiasFactCheck factual ratings (very low to very high) and NewsGuard trust scores

reported_quantity: % of patient-facing websites containing at least one statement incorrect against clinical guidelines
denominator: 39 eligible English-language patient-facing websites about metastatic renal cell carcinoma treatment, screened from the first 25 links of 36 keyword permutations across 3 search engines (2,700 queries)
misinfo_definition: "Correctness by identifying incorrect statements that were inconsistent with guidelines"; the paper frames these as "outdated, misleading, or grossly false information" and refers to "harm from misinformation"

reported_quantity: % of coded abortion-relevant YouTube comments containing potential misinformation about abortion or abortion policy
denominator: 619 abortion-relevant comments and replies from the top 20 comments (plus their replies) under the 15 YouTube clips that had more than 10 relevant comments
misinfo_definition: "potential misinformation about abortion or abortion policy which we defined as factually inaccurate medical or political content about abortion, such as abortion leading to infertility, or abortion being illegal in every U.S. state"

reported_quantity: % of surveyed breast cancer patients who reported encountering misinformation about factors purported to influence cancer progression or recurrence risk
denominator: 997 US adults with a breast cancer diagnosis within the past 10 years who completed the survey (Breastcancer.org online sample)
misinfo_definition: Medical misinformation is information that is inaccurate or misleading according to the best available evidence.

reported_quantity: % of respondents in latent class 2 who report having ever shared a political news story online that they later found out was made up (unintentional sharing)
denominator: 65 Polish active Facebook news users in latent class 2 ("The most educated users with SM literacy below average"); total sample 1,000 recruited from the largest Polish research panel
misinfo_definition: "For the purpose of this study, fake news is understood as partially or completely false information, intended to mislead the recipient, which may be intentionally and unintentionally disseminated by online news consumers"

reported_quantity: % of respondents in latent class 1 who report having ever shared a political news story online that they later found out was made up (unintentional sharing)
denominator: 96 Polish active Facebook news users in latent class 1 ("The oldest users with low SM literacy"); total sample 1,000 recruited from the largest Polish research panel
misinfo_definition: "For the purpose of this study, fake news is understood as partially or completely false information, intended to mislead the recipient, which may be intentionally and unintentionally disseminated by online news consumers"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who say at least 'some' of the news stories they encountered in online news media in the past 6 months were completely made up
denominator: 1,111 Chinese adults in a national online panel survey (Impression Boguan Network Technology / Sina Data Solution panel; cooperation rate 40.5%)
misinfo_definition: 'In this study, we define “fake news” as “news stories that are completely made up.”'

reported_quantity: % of older-adult respondents who reported encountering perceived misinformation daily
denominator: 210 Canadian adults aged 60 and over recruited via a stratified Qualtrics online panel
misinfo_definition: "misinformation--that is, false or misleading content that can have significant societal consequences"
